summary: Goose Mountain Fire Lookout, a mapped fire tower near Swan Hills, Alberta; the reserve is reached by a privately owned oilfield road, and no public source gives the tower's history or condition.

access.note: Alberta Parks says public access to the ecological reserve is by the Goose Mountain Fire Tower road from Swan Hills; the Town of Swan Hills calls that road privately owned. No source read says the public may climb the tower.

visit.trail_note: Alberta Parks: the road can be extremely difficult, especially in wet weather; no facilities; overnight camping, open fires and motorized vehicles are not permitted in the reserve.

notes_for_editor: Brief record: built 1998, height 18 m, elevation 1384.7 m and standing status come from the Alberta FRIAA WF_WILDFIRE_LOOKOUT layer, marked Protected and not for public display, so none is cited or published here. Brief access 'closed': sources say the reserve is public and reached by a private road; no source states the tower's own access, so the story does not say it is open or closed. The story does not place the tower inside the reserve; sources do not say whether it is. No built, staffing, fire or condition source found after three searches and reads. A 2006 disappearance at the Athabasca lookout near Hinton, returned by search, concerns a different tower and is not used. Alberta Parks and Town pages are undated. A YouTube video (search snippet only) calls it a fire tower; not used.
